newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end down, shrug off Hanwa Bank news.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end down, shrug off Hanwa Bank news.

text.p: Key June three-month Euroyen futures ended slightly down on Thursday, after opening higher on news that the Ministry of Finance had suspended most business of Hanwa Bank Ltd.
The June fell from that point in sympathy with the sharp decline in the key December Japanese government bond futures, after opening at the day's high of 99.24, traders said.
Key December JGB futures ended at 124.35, down sharply from Wednesday's 124.85.
The market was becoming cautious ahead of the release of the Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate sentiment survey on November 27, traders said.
"It is difficult to hold large positions in either direction ahead of the 'tankan'," a trader for a long-term credit bank said.
Comments made by Yasuo Matsushita, the BOJ governor, on Wednesday have had little effect on the market, traders said.
Matsushita told a news conference that Japan's economy is recovering gradually, with private consumption resuming a gradual recovery after being somewhat sluggish in the summer.
"The BOJ's monetary policy is geared to ensuring a firm basis for economic recovery," he said.
The weighted average of the key overnight call rate is likely to be 0.49 percent, traders said.
On Wednesday, the weighted average was 0.48 percent.
A city bank trader said the news about Hanwa Bank may have had some psychological impact on the market.

There was speculation in the market that regional banks may choose not to lend money through the overnight call market, preferring to leave funds on hand in case depositors decide to withdraw their money, the trader said.
This would lead to more competition for funds among borrowers in the overnight call market, which could cause interest rates to rise, he said.

About 60 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit were issued at 0.51 percent, and about 80 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were issued at 0.51 percent.--Tokyo Treasury Desk, +81-3-5473-3748
